judged_text: The findFirst-then-create/update sequence is not atomic (the code comment rules out upsert, but no unique constraint or transaction guards userId+appId), so two concurrent webhook deliveries both observe no existing credential and both create one. Cal.com webhook retries and concurrent sync events produce duplicate credentials for the same user+app; whichever credential the app later picks may be the stale one, and the duplicate is never reconciled.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, credentials are synchronized via a non-atomic `findFirst` (by `userId` + `appId`) followed by either `credential.update` or `credential.create`. This check-then-act pattern can race under concurrent webhook deliveries: two requests can both observe no row and both execute `create`, producing duplicates unless a DB-level unique constraint exists and is handled. The diff shows no transaction/locking, no unique constraint enforcement, and no handling of a potential unique violation on `create`.
